reason: Conversation 1 asked the right discriminating questions (clean stop vs pulsing, light pattern, model label, loose battery contacts), correctly identified SV11 as a V7, and gave honest, model-specific part advice with a sensible 'is it worth it' framing; its main weakness is that it never clearly said the cause can't be confirmed remotely or suggested Dyson diagnosis before buying. Conversation 2 opened with an unsupported overheating/airflow theory despite the customer already ruling out blockages, declared it 'almost certainly the battery' before knowing the model, then misidentified SV11 as a V8 and, when the customer explicitly asked what else to rule out, offered nothing new and no mention of Dyson support or charge-pin/body faults. Conversation 2's wrong model identification is a decisive error since it would lead to buying the wrong battery.
